messages.subject: how to set x-axis breaks in geom_motif
messages.subject_clean: how to set x-axis breaks in geom_motif
messages.body_plain:
Hi, thanks for this useful ggtree. In my case, I want to visulize several gene on my long assembled contigs. However, the contigs are very long and some genes are far away, here is the picture I draw with ggtree and geom_motif.
Here are the codes I am using.
```
virus_kofam_function <- read.delim("./ggtree.csv",sep = ',')
get_genes <- function(data, genome) {
  filter(data, viruse == genome) %>% pull(ko)
}
g <- unique(virus_kofam_function$viruse)
n <- length(g)
d <- matrix(nrow = n, ncol = n)
rownames(d) <- colnames(d) <- g
genes <- lapply(g, get_genes, data = virus_kofam_function)
for (i in 1:n) {
  for (j in 1:i) {
    jaccard_sim <- length(intersect(genes[[i]], genes[[j]])) /
      length(union(genes[[i]], genes[[j]]))
    d[j, i] <- d[i, j] <- 1 - jaccard_sim
  }
}
tree <- ape::bionj(d)
virus_kofam_N$direction <- ifelse(virus_kofam_N$direction =='+',1,-1)
virus_kofam_function$start1 <- virus_kofam_function$start
virus_kofam_function$end1 <- virus_kofam_function$end

ggtree(tree, branch.length='none',) +
  geom_tiplab(family='serif') +
  xlim_tree(20) +
  geom_facet(mapping = aes(xmin = start1, xmax = end1,
                           fill = process),
             data=virus_kofam_function, geom=geom_motif, panel='Alignment',
             on = 'nasA', label = 'ko',family = 'serif') +
  #theme(legend.position = 'none')+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")+
  theme(text = element_text(family = 'serif',color = 'black'))+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3")
```
The data I am using is attached.
Is there a way to only show the area in my .csv table or to set break?

messages.subject: Branch superposition ggtree
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am new to this group, I did check but did not found reply to my question here, sorry if it has been asked before.

I have a problem of branch superposition while plotting my tree. Not sure about the wording, but see attach my problem with for instance the branch of Strix_chacoensis superposing the branch of the other Strix. How can I deal with that ?

Here below my code (not run):

data.owl <- read.table("data.owl.txt", h=T)

owl.tree.final = read.nexus("owl.tree.final")
svl <- data.owl$Max.bino
names(svl) = data.owl$Species
fit <- phytools::fastAnc(owl.tree.final, svl, vars=TRUE, CI=TRUE)

td <- data.frame(node = nodeid(owl.tree.final, names(svl)),
                 trait = svl)
nd <- data.frame(node = names(fit$ace), trait = fit$ace)

d <- rbind(td, nd)
d$node <- as.numeric(d$node)
tree <- full_join(owl.tree.final, d, by = 'node')

p1 <- ggtree(tree, aes(color=trait), layout = 'rectangular',
             ladderize = FALSE, continuous = 'colour', size=2) +

  scale_color_gradientn(colours=c("red", 'orange', 'green', 'cyan', 'blue')) +
  geom_tiplab(hjust = -.1) +
  xlim(0, 80) +
  theme(legend.position = c(.05, .85))

p1

Best regards,

Simon Potier
